players.product: AI data-center colocation (Tydal, Norway: 121 IT MW leased to Volta for NVIDIA GPUs) and Bitdeer AI GPU cloud (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 / Vera Rubin capacity in Malaysia, Norway and the US)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (20-F): revenue increased by 77.3% from US$349.8 million in 2024 to US$620.3 million in 2025, primarily driven by a significant increase in self-mining revenue and sale of mining rigs and accessories. AI cloud services revenue increased by 96.2% from US$3.5 million to US$6.8 million, primarily due to the expansion of GPU server deployment and increased customer demand for AI computing services; the colocation business has not yet generated any revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue US$620.3 million (+77.3%); AI cloud services US$6.8 million (+96.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 revenue concentration (20-F; customers not named): Customer B 16.65%, Customer C 15.81%, Customer D 12.20% and Customer E 10.28% of revenue in 2025 (each below 10% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: Customer B 16.65%; Customer C 15.81%; Customer D 12.20%; Customer E 10.28% (FY2025)

quarterly_data.signal: AI cloud GPU fleet (20-F): as of December 31, 2025 Bitdeer had procured or placed orders for AI cloud equipment from certain suppliers with a total purchase amount of approximately US$56.0 million - NVIDIA DGX H100 (31 servers), NVIDIA H200 (3), NVIDIA B200 (4), NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 (8), NVIDIA B300 (16) and NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (2); 2,128 GPUs were deployed as of March 31, 2026. GPUs are bought from certain GPU suppliers and OEMs through individual purchase orders, with no long-term supply agreements guaranteeing capacity, pricing or payment terms.
quarterly_data.figure: ~US$56.0 million of NVIDIA AI cloud servers procured or ordered; 2,128 GPUs deployed (March 31, 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Datacenter portfolio as of March 31, 2026 (20-F): ten datacenters with 1,744.0 MW of electrical capacity in use plus 1,259.5 MW of pipeline, for approximately 3,003.5 MW in total. Mining sites being converted: Knoxville, Tennessee to AI cloud in two phases (37 MW targeted Q4 2026, 49 MW Q1 2027); Wenatchee, Washington 13 MW to AI cloud (Q4 2026, starting with a GB300 cluster); Tydal, Norway (50 MW and 175 MW) to colocation around the end of 2026, with Data Center Installations AS as design and construction partner. Pipeline: Niles, Ohio 300 MW grid-interconnected site for colocation / AI cloud (Q4 2028); Clarington, Ohio 570 MW of power under contract with a local utility, intended for colocation (timing may be affected by legal proceedings filed by American Heavy Plate Solutions); Rockdale, Texas additional 179 MW (2026) under evaluation for colocation / AI cloud; Cyberjaya, Malaysia 9.5 MW of leased AI cloud capacity (Q4 2026). Average datacenter electricity cost approximately US$45/MWh in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,744.0 MW in use; 1,259.5 MW pipeline; ~3,003.5 MW total; ~US$45/MWh (2025)
